node.title: DLI primitive joint-ratio telescoping identity
node.statement: Let t=2^m and use the exact U-weighted dyadic tower. Write Z_j for the weighted level-j null census, B_j for the unconditional junction-j block census, and C_1 for the first saturated/coset census. Then C_1=Z_0(q,n/2,t/2), Z_0-C_1 is the all-weight primitive t-null count, and the primitive joint-to-marginal ratio is J_prim=2^(nm)(Z_0-C_1)/(Z_m product_(j<m) B_j). Equivalently, when Z_0>C_1, log2 J_prim=R3_full+log2(1-C_1/Z_0). The central primitive C2'' ratio is at most J_prim, so J_prim<=2^21 is a sufficient exact integer form of C2''.
node.attack_surface: Check the tower normalization, first saturated-column ownership, terminal factor, junction index range, and central-to-all-weight domination.
node.falsifier: A dyadic tower where the primitive count is not Z_0-C_1, the displayed ratio disagrees with direct joint/marginal normalization, or the central primitive submass exceeds the all-weight primitive mass.
node.notes: This converts the repaired target to one positive integer inequality. It does not prove that inequality on official rows. The 45-row exact replay is stress evidence only.
